x: Over this stretch of 31 miles odd, Lloyd Johnson (Leicester), Whitlock (Metropolitan W.C.) and our own warrior, Fred Rickards, had a great battle.
Approaching Croydon, Whitlock drew level with Stone, and shortly afterwards went ahead. Even at this early stage it was evident that Ludlow's record was in danger.
Whitlock and Hopkins made clear their claims beyond any shadow of doubt, and T. Lloyd Johnson, although failing on this occasion, has sterling performances to his credit in the past.
Even Whitlock was 17 seconds slower; all of which shows that Tommy is very far from being the spent force some people would like us to believe.

Whitlock (Metropolitan W.C.) leading the field home For once in a while the newspapers gave a little publicity to our sport, and Whitlock himself received a great ovation on arriving home, as was his due.

Our visitor began to fall back at seven miles, however, leaving Harold Whitlock in the lead, which he retained to the end. At Redhill, Whitlock was two and a half minutes in front of record, and gained yet another minute before Horley was reached.
Eventually Whitlock's superior knowledge of the course, over which he has won many races, prevailed and enabled him to beat Fred by something under 100 yards.

Meanwhile, Harold Whitlock had been gaining places and eventually beat our Joe by a small margin. An attempt to total the team scores at six miles (approx.) showed that we were scoring 35 points to the 36 of the Metropolitan W.C.!
Amongst the most noteworthy Club performances during the season are those of Jack Rutland, second to Whitlock in the Woodford Green Open and again second to Burgess in our own open.
To go to the head of the field and win the race and to be acclaimed with the names of Whitlock, Baker, Thompson, Pamich, Middleton is something extra.

His interest had been sparked by the "Kings of Speed" cigarette card series which featured Wooderson, Whitlock, Owens, etc.; and when he heard that Wooderson was to run at Tooting Bec in a ¾ mile record attempt he cycled there especially to witness one of his heroes.
